item.title: Version 2.0.0-beta.2
item.description:
PrismPack 2.0.0 beta 2. Fixes from the first beta.

  • One copy, always the newest. Starting PrismPack a second time shows the first copy's window. Starting a newer build closes the older one, so there is never a second menu bar icon or window.
  • Homebrew apps that wouldn't update. Apps Homebrew can't replace on its own (owned by another user or by root) used to fail again and again in the background. They now wait for you and ask for your password when you press Update. A leftover copy from an earlier failed upgrade gets a Repair and Update button, and the failure shows Homebrew's real message. If an automatic update hits one, a notification tells you.
  • No endless retries. After two failures in a row, automatic updates stop trying that app until a new version arrives. Updating by hand still works.
  • One password prompt, and it says why. Both password prompts are now the same native alert, and say what the password is for and what set it off, for example "to update Signal, which you started". Skip is now Cancel.
  • Notifications have Open and Dismiss buttons, and are removed from Notification Center once you use them.
  • Daily cleanup. Clears Homebrew's old versions and downloads, and the pip and npm caches. It runs at most once every 23 hours: with the first background check after that, or about 45 seconds after PrismPack starts if one is due (it needs the background check on or PrismPack open). Each run is logged in Activity as "Daily cleanup" with what it freed. Nothing you installed is removed, and you can turn it off in Settings.
  • Set up window. The first launch opens a Set up window: Homebrew and mas first, then optional Full Disk Access with what it is for. Settings shows "Granted" with how to turn it off, and the wording follows your macOS version.
  • Look-alikes. Apps that share one bundle ID but have different names (such as two editions of one product) are shown as look-alikes, with nothing suggested to remove.
  • Check for Updates moved to the PrismPack section at the top of Settings.

Full Disk Access on macOS 27.3 is still in beta. Apple changed how it works in the 27.3 beta (a new list, adding apps with + instead of dragging, and optional folder-by-folder access). PrismPack's steps for 27.3 may change until 27.3 is released. macOS 15 and 26 are unchanged.

This is a beta. Full details are on the GitHub release page.

item.title: Version 2.0.0-beta.1
item.description:
PrismPack 2.0 beta. UpdateScout is now PrismPack, and it does much more than update.

  • New name, same app. Your settings, history, hidden lists and background check carry over. The app renames itself to PrismPack.app, and because macOS sees a new app it asks again for notifications and Full Disk Access (optional).
  • A new window: a sidebar with Updates, Installed, Orphaned App Files, Discover, Activity and Settings, in the Liquid Glass look on macOS 26 and later (simpler on macOS 15). Cards or a list on the main pages.
  • Discover: find and install new apps, tools, fonts and extensions from Homebrew, npm, PyPI, crates.io, RubyGems and the editor stores, with descriptions, pictures and font previews.
  • More updates: Python (pipx and uv), npm, Rust, Ruby gems, VS Code, VSCodium and Cursor extensions, Apple's own apps through Software Update, and your own sources.
  • Faster, clearer installs: several updates at once, one password per batch, and a progress bar with a percent and a step line.
  • Installed, Duplicates and Uninstall: everything on your Mac in one list, two copies of an app compared side by side, and removal to the Trash with the files an app left behind.
  • Orphaned App Files and optional Full Disk Access to clear what macOS protects.
  • You decide: Stable or Beta per app, automatic updates (off until you turn them on), and more ways to hide updates.
  • Settings: search, a tool list with Install and Reinstall, and release notes for every version.
  • Light on memory: about 15 MB in the menu bar, and closing the window frees much of what it was using.

This is a beta. Full details are on the GitHub release page.

item.title: Version 1.8.0
item.description:
A menu bar that stays current

  • The menu bar count now updates on its own when a background check finishes, without clicking the icon.
  • New menu bar icons: a spinner while checking, the arrows with a count when updates are available, and a checkmark when everything is up to date.

Review major upgrades

  • Update All no longer installs major-version jumps silently. A review sheet lists them with their release notes, and each one is opt-in.
  • Tick "I've reviewed these" to Proceed, or choose Skip these, update the rest.

Release tracks

  • Apps on a beta or alpha are kept on that track, and stable apps are only offered stable releases.
  • Updates that need a newer macOS than yours are no longer offered.
  • More accurate version comparison (for example, 3.0.0 now ranks above 3.0.0-beta.4).

Safety and reliability

  • If the driver check fails, no drivers are listed as safe to remove, and removing one now asks first.
  • The password prompt says what it is for.
  • Cancel now stops app downloads, and an app that won't quit is no longer replaced while running.
  • Fixed the background check and the app overwriting each other's results.

Note: ignored and already-notified updates reset once with this version.

item.title: Version 1.7.2
item.description: • The Repair button is now text only, so its label is no longer cut off to "Re…" on the narrow update cards.

item.title: Version 1.7.1
item.description:
Repair for stuck Homebrew upgrades

If a Homebrew cask upgrade was ever interrupted, Homebrew leaves the old version in a leftover .upgrading folder, and every later update fails with "It seems there is already an App at…".

  • UpdateScout now recognises this and explains it in plain English.
  • The failed card shows a Repair button. It moves the leftover folder to the Trash (recoverable, never deleted) and reinstalls the app cleanly.

item.title: Version 1.7.0
item.description:
A new look

  • New app icon, built in Icon Composer and rendered natively with Liquid Glass (no more grey legacy frame in the Dock).
  • Frosted title sheet across the top of the window, with the logo, version, settings and Check Now.
  • Sections are floating panels that roll smoothly open and closed. Each has its own Update button, and remembers whether you collapsed it.
  • Cards keep a fixed size and reflow with the window; the default window fits three across.

Updates

  • macOS updates open Software Update in System Settings instead of installing directly.
  • App Store: apps UpdateScout can update keep their own cards; only the ones that need the App Store are grouped into a single Open App Store card.
  • Check for updates as often as every 5 minutes.

Settings

  • Version and Check for Updates at the top of Settings, which now opens centred on the main window.
  • New Glass slider from Clear to Opaque, and a smooth crossfade when switching light and dark.

Fixes

  • Collapsing a section near the bottom no longer makes the list jump.
  • Sharper logos, a clearer password dialog, and readable section counts in dark mode.
